_note: Draft content lifted from the mockup. Matrix notes are unverified until each claim has a primary source. Status codes: M measured, C cited, P partial match, B breaks here, N not assessed. Sites with no counterpart location are hidden by the page. Rio Tinto and Yungay were added with sources named in each site's data field; blank cells are Not assessed, not guesses.

sites.name: Kamestastin Lake impact structure
sites.helps: Crew geology training on anorthosite impact rocks; traverse planning on crater terrain of similar size.
sites.data: Copernicus DEM GLO-30, LRO LOLA, Earth Impact Database

geo: Formed in anorthosite, the main rock of the lunar highlands
terrain: Relief, slope and roughness on one 80 m grid
temp: Subarctic; nothing like polar cold traps or low sun
ice: A lake and seasonal snow, not cold-trapped ice
dust: Soil and glacial deposits, not regolith
ops: Share of ground gentle enough to land and drive

sites.cmpNote: Anchor and analog wording is taken from this site's existing notes; it is not yet independently sourced.

sites.name: Sittampundi anorthosite complex
sites.novelty: Studied as simulant, not as a field site
sites.helps: Source rock for lunar soil simulant used in landing and rover tests.

geo: Simulant oxides close to highland anorthosite
dust: Crushed rock stands in for regolith in tests
ops: Bulk simulant for landing and wheel tests

sites.name: Umm Jirsan lava tube
sites.novelty: Less studied as an analog (check pending)
sites.helps: Testing skylight entry, cave mapping and radio relay underground.

geo: Basalt tube; the lunar pit is in mare basalt
sub: Tube 8 to 12 m high; lunar pit far larger

sites.name: Galena Creek rock glacier
sites.helps: Radar tests of how thick the debris over buried ice is, which sets how reachable the water is.
sites.data: Published radar; SHARAD; Copernicus DEM and MOLA (possible)

temp: Warmer, with liquid water in summer
ice: Ice under 1 to 1.5 m of debris, estimated 80 to 95% pure
sub: Buried ice body sounded by radar
ops: Radar method for finding drillable ice

sites.name: Great Kobuk Sand Dunes
sites.helps: Watching dunes move from orbit; driving on frozen sand.
sites.data: ASTER time series; Mars dataset not yet chosen

temp: Snow-covered for most of the year
dust: Dunes moved about 1.3 m a year, 2003 to 2008
bio: Liquid water persists under the dunes
ops: Change detection and mobility on frozen sand

sites.name: Bodélé Depression
sites.target: Dust lifting (a process, no single site)
sites.novelty: Less studied as a Mars analog (check pending)
sites.helps: Testing dust-emission models and storm forecasting.
sites.data: MODIS aerosol optical depth; Mars Climate Sounder

dust: About half the dust that leaves the Sahara
bio: The dust itself is from water life

sites.name: Lake Salda
sites.helps: Recognising carbonate deposits and planning where to look for biosignatures.

geo: Magnesium carbonates, as found at Jezero
bio: Living lake: tests biosignature strategy, not ancient Mars

sites.name: Río Tinto mining district
sites.helps: Practice reading iron-sulfate rocks like those at Meridiani Planum, including how traces of life survive in them.
sites.data: Fernandez-Remolar et al. 2005, Earth and Planetary Science Letters 240. Terrain not yet run. Coordinates: Minas de Riotinto town (Wikipedia); Meridiani about 2 S, 5.9 W (approximate, NASA/JPL summaries).

geo: Iron-rich jarosite and hematite deposits, a partial sedimentary analog of the Meridiani rocks (Fernandez-Remolar et al. 2005)
bio: Traces of microbial life preserved as textures in iron oxides: a test for reading Mars outcrops (Fernandez-Remolar et al. 2005)

sites.name: Yungay area, Atacama Desert
sites.helps: Tests whether Viking-type instruments would find organics in very dry, oxidising soil.
sites.data: Navarro-Gonzalez et al. 2003, Science (Mars-like soils in the Atacama). Terrain not yet run. Atacama point is the regional point from our site list; Yungay coordinates to be confirmed. Viking 1: JPL Photojournal 22.48 N, 49.97 W (sources differ by up to about 0.4 deg).

geo: Very dry, salty soils with almost no organic matter; called Mars-like (Navarro-Gonzalez et al. 2003)
ice: Driest core of the Atacama; dry enough to limit microbial life (Navarro-Gonzalez et al. 2003)
bio: Almost no culturable microbes; soil breaks organics down without life (Navarro-Gonzalez et al. 2003)

earth.name: Earth
earth.desc: Our test bench. Each site here matches the Moon or Mars in some measured or documented ways and differs in others.
earth.sitesHead: Earth sites and processes in this atlas
earth.limit: Liquid water, weather and life act on every Earth site and alter it in ways the Moon and Mars do not.

moon.name: Moon
moon.desc: Airless and grey, with highlands of pale anorthosite and craters that have barely eroded in billions of years. The south pole is where Artemis plans to land.
moon.limit: One sixth of Earth gravity, a vacuum, unshielded radiation, and the cold and lighting of polar craters. No Earth site matches these.

mars.name: Mars
mars.desc: A cold desert with a thin carbon dioxide atmosphere, buried ice, dune fields and old lake beds that record a wetter past.
mars.limit: About a third of Earth gravity, air under 1% as dense, high radiation and no liquid water at the surface today.

pairs.otherTitle: de Gerlache crater, lunar south pole

controls.text: Crater against crater should score alike

operations: Share of each window gentle enough to land on and drive across, using a published slope limit (to be looked up and cited). A training site with a similar share lets crews and rovers practise on comparable ground.
breaks: Shape only. Gravity, vacuum, temperature, lighting and erosion all differ, and the elevation model cannot see under the lake or the forest.
imagery: Imagery: NASA GIBS Blue Marble; LRO WAC global mosaic and Viking MDIM 2.1 colour mosaic through NASA Trek. NASA is acknowledged as the source and does not endorse this project.
